chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My father said to me, 'O Ja'far, set aside for me such and such from my wealth for wailing women who will wail for me for ten years in Mina, during the days of Mina.'

key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina, a sacred site near Mecca associated with Hajj rituals
key_terms.عَشْرَ سِنِينَ: Ten years, indicating the duration of the mourning service
key_terms.نَوَادِبَ: Professional wailing women hired to mourn the dead

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir instruct his son Ja'far to do regarding hiring wailing women for mourning?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practice of *nawadib* (professional female mourners) in early Shia tradition, where Imam al-Baqir commissioned them to lament his death in Mina for ten years, blending pre-Islamic customs with Islamic piety. While later jurists debated the permissibility of hiring mourners versus natural grief, this narration highlights the social significance of public mourning as a means of honoring the Ahl al-Bayt and maintaining their legacy during the Hajj season.
